summary:
This is a little follow-up note to my letter of yesterday. Long time ago—yearswhen I first talked to you on the phone, when I had just joined the Doubleday list, you said to me in a sort of wondering but wistful voice, “I guess you’re not as well-known as Heinlein.” I had to admit I wasn’t. HOWEVER (this is the best I can do to make up for that, and it’s taken a while). When Harley Cokliss of the B.B.C. flew here to interview and film sci­ ence fiction writers for a one-to-two hour film for the B.B.C. TV, on the West Coast he asked to see only three writers: Ray Bradbury, Harlan Ellison, and me. (On the East Coast he filmed Vonnegut and Fred Pohl and I forget who else. Blish. In the U.K., Ballard and Aldiss.) Anyhow, my then fiancee Tessa said to 

 219 Cokliss, “I guess you filmed Ray Bradbury because he’s the first name that comes to mind in England when someone thinks of science fiction.” Mr. Cokliss said, “Oh, miss; I would say that the name Philip K. Dick comes to mind first, equally, regarding science fiction; I would certainly say that.” Cokliss also told me that the rock magazine Rolling Stones printed an item, evidendy recently, about John Lennon of the Beatles being interested in THE THREE STIGMATA OF PALMER ELDRITCH, evidently for a possible movie. The other HOWEVER (it’s always good to have two howevers) comes from France. My Editions Opta editor Patrice Duvic, who came to the LA.
